about: A bow: a wooden stave with a string, held in the off hand and drawn by the main hand. Today it shoots arrows as a tool, with no draw of its own.

hands.source: holding.md section 1: a bow is held in two hands, Two, the off hand leading

lead.source: holding.md's lead (Off for a bow) and attach_kinds.json's bow lead; the right on a left-handed body (D463)

grip_type.source: D562: in hand, a power grip closed by touch on the riser

slots.name: stave
slots.joins: its frame's origin is the grip on the riser; its two nocks are full points the string runs between

slots.name: string
slots.joins: a straight cord at rest from nock.lower to nock.upper, its diameter the nocks' size

slots.name: grip_wrap
slots.joins: its bore round the riser at the grip, the riser's section there

grip.how: the stave's grip point on the riser, 4.5 cm under its middle so the arrow rests on the fist (bow.json's grip): the item's origin, +Y toward the upper nock, the string toward +Z

second.how: nock, the string's middle at rest: the midpoint of the stave's two nock points (the string is straight between them), which the drawing hand takes (attachment.md Second grip)

edge.how: a bow does not strike; what it shoots leaves from the nock point along the arrow's line

held.how: in the off hand's socket, with no ready pose

open.why: a bow's ready hold and draw are not built (holding.md section 3: the bow, not built)

used.how: as a tool today it shoots on a held button (items.ron tool.shoots), with no draw clip

open.why: the draw: the string's middle follows the main hand while drawn, the hand on the clip (holding.md section 3), not built

carried.how: today tipped by the carry rule as any look in hand

open.why: how a bow is carried: the review desk's bow-carry item is unanswered

stowed.how: across the back, beside a shield there

open.why: the turn and offset on the socket are not set (attachment.md Stowed's next step); the quiver on the back's spine (D551) must leave it room

blocking.how: a bow does not block; holding.md's Two stance blocks with the weapon, which a bow's set will replace with its draw

open.why: bow.two (holding.md's count) with its draw, keyed with both hands

length_m.source: art/held/bow.json length; the look's bounds measured 1.200

mass_kg.source: a wooden self bow of 1.2 m (recalled: 0.5 to 0.7 kg); a stand-in

open.why: a bow has no head: the stave is the whole; mass matters to its draw, not a swing

balance_m.source: the stave's middle 4.5 cm above the grip (bow.json)

open.why: D459's tempo is a swing's; what bounds a bow comes with its draw clips
the riser is not round; its section is the stave's, measured when made
a bow is drawn, not swung; D459's tempo clamp does not bound it

length_m.source: the reference's length ±10%, so the drawing hand's reach to the nock stays the clips' (research section 3's IK budget, a few centimetres); D546's bow range is 1.0 to 1.9 m

open.why: not a swing's; bounded, if at all, by the draw clips

envelope.state: only the length is bounded, and only as a stand-in: the draw's clips set the rest
